prompt:
I need the front end for Backpack Notes. A family messaging app that collects school communication for a household (teacher notes, office announcements, co-parent and caregiver messages) in one place, tied to each child.

Who's using it: Priya Raman, 41, a hospital pharmacist and mother of two who shares custody with her ex-husband, Vikram. Her mother, Lakshmi, does Tuesday and Thursday pickups. Priya handles most school correspondence, usually late at night.

What they're doing right now: It's 9:45 pm Tuesday. Her 9th grader Anika's chemistry teacher wrote that three lab reports are missing and asked for a conference this week. Priya needs to reply with times that work, bring Vikram in since Anika is at his place Wednesday through Friday, and check with Anika what's going on. Separately, her 3rd grader Rohan's teacher asked why his reading log hasn't been signed for two weeks. Lakshmi had messaged earlier that she signed it but Rohan may have left it in her car. Priya wants to answer both teachers tonight without repeating herself or contradicting what Vikram already told the school.

What's in the system at this point: Children: Anika (9th grade, Northgate High, 7 teachers) and Rohan (3rd grade, Pinecrest Elementary, teacher Ms. Delacroix). There are 14 unread messages across 6 conversations. Mr. Okafor (Anika's chemistry teacher) wrote Monday 3:12 pm, listing Labs 4, 5 and 6 as missing with due dates of 21 Oct, 4 Nov and 14 Nov and proposing Thursday 3:30 or Friday 7:45 am. Vikram wrote to Mr. Okafor on 9 Nov, saying Anika 'was catching up' (Priya was copied). Ms. Delacroix wrote today at 2:05 pm about the reading log for the weeks of 3 and 10 Nov. Lakshmi wrote at 5:40 pm: 'Signed his log, in my car I think.' The Pinecrest office announced a picture retake on 2 Dec. The custody schedule shows Anika with Vikram Wed–Fri this week. Each message has a sender, a role (teacher, office, co-parent, grandparent, child), a child it's tagged to, and read and replied status.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
